direction.premise: A tiny tin robot barrels through a mechanical test rig while a pair of operators fight over two chunky industrial pushbuttons.
direction.composition: Edge-to-edge painted workshop diorama above a single shared lower metal control face; on portrait phones the camera follows the robot while the progress track remains visible.
direction.shapeLanguage: Pressed steel trays, machined circles, exposed bolts, enamel strips and two large plunger switches. Nothing is floating in a generic card grid.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Painted iron, rubbed aluminum edges, amber enamel, rubber wheels and dusty machine-green workshop panels. All distinct from paper/ink media in neighboring apps.
direction.paletteLogic: The world uses subdued sage and petroleum hues, the control deck graphite, jump honey-yellow and reversal desaturated cobalt; warnings have rust-orange accents.
direction.typography: Compressed mechanical display heading, monospaced instrument legends, and readable sentence-case functional paragraphs.
direction.signature: The only two key controls are full-size physical plungers that visually sink on contact while a tiny metal character reacts inside the stage.
direction.distinction: Unlike axis-pals's grid transport, this is continuous momentum and platform contact; unlike crumple-yard's vehicle sandbox, it is side-view two-action shared control.

architecture.primaryVerb: Time jumps and reverse the autonomous Boltik to cross four metal platforms and reach the goal.
architecture.physicalFeedback: The jump injects vertical velocity, the reversal changes motor facing, and impacts move the character and nudge the scene.
architecture.spatialRationale: The scene owns all flexible space; the two touch controls keep fixed size and safe-area distance, and overlays replace it only between runs.

comparisons.spatialDifference: One continuous side-scrolling world above the plunger deck instead of a warehouse grid.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Two real-time impulses steer a single autonomous body rather than discrete simultaneous moves of two actors.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Side-view toy test rig rather than 3D crash-yard driving camera.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Players share two limited impulses, rather than one player driving continuously and deforming a car.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Rigid instrument enclosure replaces painting studio and tool shelf.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Fixed-timestep physical impulses replace freehand painter input.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Controlled factory silhouettes replace particle trajectories in open laboratory.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Two operators trigger discrete motion corrections rather than emitting continuous trajectories.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Mechanical rail and robot replace miniature greens and putting camera.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Motor and jump cooperate on landing control, rather than ball aim and momentum-only golf.

production.renderer: Deterministic Canvas 2D geometric illustration with a device-scale backing buffer and fixed-update kinematics.
production.focalAsset: Bolтик is original procedural robot geometry with visible tire axles, blinking optics, antenna and enamel shell; icons are an original SVG pushbutton.

motion.character: Heavy plunger presses and springy robot chassis, without constant decorative shaking.
motion.action: Press jump or reverse, observe the corresponding vector change immediately.
motion.anticipation: The autonomous robot approaches a clear vertical obstacle while the chosen action remains available.
motion.response: Press deformation in the first frame; simulated impulse in the next 1/120-second tick.
motion.followThrough: Robot and camera settle from physical trajectory, button returns to its rest position.
motion.interruption: The next input takes priority; pausing halts the simulation and releases the buttons.
motion.reducedMotion: Reduced-motion CSS removes decorative transitions while position/contact and button state remain informative.
motion.physicalFeedback: Events from the physics engine trigger subtle landed impact and procedural clicks.

evidence.expectedChange: The launch panel closes, robot starts moving automatically and two operator plungers become active.
